description.p: Callie is a calendar for people who live in their calendar. It connects to Google Calendar and any CalDAV server, and gives you day, week, month and agenda views that are quick to read and quick to change.

ul.li: Google Calendar and CalDAV accounts
Day, week, month and agenda views
Drag to reschedule, drag to create
Natural-language quick add
Desktop notifications with one-click join for video calls
A companion command-line interface for power users

Reminders come without the app: the terminal calendar notifies while it is open, and callie reminders runs on its own, as from a systemd user service. Only one of them and the app reminds at a time, so none comes twice.

The terminal calendar's typed lines edit as in a shell, with the arrows, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-E, Ctrl-W and Ctrl-U, and Up and Down bring back earlier ones. A search shows what it finds as it is typed, Tab completes a calendar's name, and : runs a command such as :week or :add.
The terminal calendar goes to a day with gd or :go, repeats a move given a count, as 3l, moves half a screen with Ctrl-D and Ctrl-U, and shows an agenda of any length with :agenda 30.
The terminal calendar has a month view: the month's weeks, each day with its first events and how many more it has, opened with the leader then m, as in the app, or :month.

The terminal calendar can show days and weeks as an hour grid, with each event at its time and a line at the current time, switched with the leader then g or :grid and kept in Settings. In the week's grid, j and k stay within a day, and H and L go to the day before or after.
In the terminal calendar, Tab on a new event's line adds it and opens its fields, which now take its repeat, guests, video call and notes too, as well as its title, place, times and calendar.
An event's details in the terminal calendar open its place in a map with M and its page with O, and copy its call's link, or its page's, with c.
callie next prints the event on now, or the next, in one line for a status bar such as waybar, polybar or tmux, or as JSON with --json.
In the terminal calendar, deleting asks first, and deleting or answering an event that repeats asks whether it is for this occurrence or all of them.

The terminal calendar and the app read their keys from one table, so what both do takes the same keys: the app's leader keys work in the terminal, as leader then i for invitations and leader then r to sync, and the terminal's help lists them all.

The terminal calendar can change events: e lists an event's title, place, times, all-day and calendar to change one by one, m moves it to a time typed, keeping its length, y and p copy it onto another day, and D duplicates it. Each change can be taken back with u.
Callie has Arch Linux packages, in each release and in the Greylock Labs repository.
The installer sets Callie up on Arch and the systems built on it, other than Manjaro.
The sync button's arrow glyph has been improved visually.

settings.ini now holds only preferences, so it can be copied or synced to another computer as it is. What belongs to this computer goes in local.ini beside it: hidden calendars, the names and colors you gave calendars and accounts, folded accounts, the calendar new events go into, connected Zoom accounts, the last view shown and the last version run. After upgrading, those start fresh.
Callie's wording lives in translations/callie_en.ts, where it can be changed without touching the code, ready for other languages to sit beside it.
Answering or changing one occurrence of a Google series that its organizer split with "this and following" no longer fails with "Not Found".
Google's holiday calendars, which refuse to sync incrementally, are read in full every six hours instead of on every sync.
Settings' tabs line up under its title, with more room between them.

Settings lists its tabs down the left and keeps one size, scrolling a tab only when the window is too small for it. Calendars on this computer, subscriptions and importing have a Calendars tab, and Zoom and the join card a Video calls tab.

Each account takes one line in Settings, with Reconnect and Remove under its "..." button and a line of its own only when something needs seeing to. One Connect an account button offers Google, Microsoft and CalDAV.
Guests can be optional. Click a guest in the editor to make them optional, or required again; the event's details mark who is optional. callie edit --optional names them from the terminal.

Events can move to another calendar, from Calendar under More options in the editor or with callie edit --calendar. A repeating event moves as a whole series. Within one Google account, guests keep their invitations; elsewhere, an event with guests stays where it is.

Zoom can make the meetings for events instead of Google Meet or Teams. Connect Zoom under Video calls in Settings, and the video call switch makes a Zoom meeting and puts its link in Where. Connect several Zoom accounts, and each event's meeting is made as the one with its calendar's account's email, or the one chosen for other calendars.
Changes made to a new event before Callie's next sync, such as renaming it or adding guests, are no longer lost with a sync failure.
An event drawn over one you cannot edit, such as one on a calendar shared with you, can be dragged again instead of showing that it cannot move.
A repeating all-day event on a local, subscribed, CalDAV or Microsoft calendar keeps its last day west of UTC, where it used to end a day early.
The box for renaming or recoloring a calendar stays inside the window, instead of running off the bottom when opened from a calendar low in the sidebar.
Short events next to each other in the week can be clicked and dragged by their middle again: their edges for changing the time no longer cover the whole event.

A card in the corner of the window offers to join the current or next call, from a few minutes before it starts until it ends, using the same link as the event's Join button. Its X hides it for that call only, and Settings › Reminders can turn it off.
Callie Light's pink is deeper, with white text on it, so buttons and what is selected are easier to read.
Choosing a file or folder opens your desktop's own file chooser, with its places and bookmarks, rather than a plain one of its own.

An event moved to another week or month, by dragging it to the edge or by changing its date, shows in its new place straight away. It used to vanish for several seconds, until the change reached the server.

Short events in the week and day views are tidier: a run of them back to back, such as two 15-minute tasks, are drawn the same size with an even gap between them, the title is centered, and the start time shows beside it when there is room.

An event's title, time, details, guests and notes can be selected and copied from its card: drag or double-click, then Ctrl+C, or right-click for Copy. Long notes show in full, and the card scrolls when they make it taller than the window.

Short events back to back, such as 11:45 to 12:00 and then 12:00 to 12:15, sit one above the other at full width, as their times do, rather than side by side. Events only share the width when their times overlap.

Google and Microsoft events have "Open in Google Calendar" or "Open in Outlook" on their card, which opens the event's own page on the web, in the right Google account. Callie downloads Google events once more after updating, to learn their pages.
The date picker's month arrows go to the next and previous month again; west of UTC, Next stayed put and Previous skipped a month.

Copying or moving an event to a time you picked no longer fails on a Google calendar with "Missing time zone definition for start time". New events on CalDAV and local calendars keep this computer's time zone too, instead of floating to whoever opens them.
A change that a calendar turned down no longer leaves the sync status failed until the next change; the next sync clears it.

The video call switch in the editor says what it makes, such as "Add a Google Meet", and notes when Where already has a link. Join opens a call link typed in Where ahead of a meeting the calendar added, and knows SimplePractice, Doxy.me, Whereby, Jitsi Meet and GoTo Meeting links.
"Report a problem" in the ? menu files a bug or an idea as a public GitHub issue without a GitHub account, and shows the diagnostics it includes before you send them.
callie donate opens Callie's Ko-fi page, and --print prints its link instead.

Callie's own package repository at callieapp.org, which the Greylock Labs repository replaced in 0.5.8. If /etc/yum.repos.d/callie.repo or /etc/apt/sources.list.d/callie.sources is still there, remove it and run the installer again to add the Greylock Labs repository.

The installer adds the Greylock Labs repository at <https://packages.greylocklabs.org>, which carries Callie and Jot, in place of Callie's own, and removes the old one. Machines that already have Callie's repository keep getting updates from it.
Callie's source and releases moved to <https://github.com/greylocklabs/callie>. Updates, the installer and bug reports use the new address; the old one redirects there.
Themes made in Jot, with its [editor] section for the note editor's font and code colors, load without warnings; Callie keeps the section and does not use it.
Opening Callie from its tray entry brings the window to the front on Wayland, as Plasma asks.
An account's photo in Settings, under Accounts, draws without errors, and an account without one shows its letter.
Packages for Ubuntu 26.04 or later, built against Ubuntu's own libraries. The installer and callie upgrade pick them on Ubuntu, and Callie's apt repository has them under its own suite.
The keyboard shortcuts window and the theme editor open again; they showed only the dimmed window behind them.
Every dialog and popup has an X that closes it, as Escape does.

Callie has its own signed dnf and apt repository at callieapp.org. The installer adds it, so later updates come with dnf upgrade or apt upgrade; run it again to add it to an existing install. The README shows how to add it by hand.
When Google or Microsoft turns a sync request down, the log says which request it was and the reason the server gave, not only the status code.
With Qt 6.12, a sign-in that Google or Microsoft turns down says why again, such as invalid_grant, rather than only "Bad Request".
callie --help keeps a space between each command and its description, where unsubscribe ran into its own, and callie completions without a shell says how to use it.
Shell completion offers --help and --version.
On GNOME, a button layout with no window buttons, as tiling setups often use, is followed rather than putting minimize, maximize and close back.
Copying a theme under a name with a line break in it no longer leaves a theme that will not load.
Turning debug logging on or off while Callie is busy can no longer upset the check that keeps event details out of the log file.

Outlook and Microsoft 365 accounts: connect one in Settings, under Accounts, or with callie accounts add microsoft. Calendars sync both ways, guests get invitations from Outlook, invitations can be answered, and events can have a Teams link where the account has Teams.
Make and delete calendars on CalDAV servers, under the account in Settings or with callie calendars new <name> --account <id> and callie calendars remove. Deleting asks first.
Save a calendar, or one event, as an .ics file from the calendar's menu in the sidebar or the event's details, or with callie export.
Importing an .ics file into Google keeps a changed occurrence of a repeating event in its series.
The end time list says how long the event would be: it counted a quarter hour short.

description.p: Renaming and recoloring CalDAV calendars on the server, invitations sent by CalDAV servers, .ics files imported into CalDAV and Google calendars, and flat grey disabled buttons.
CalDAV accounts such as Fastmail, iCloud and Nextcloud, calendars kept on this computer, adding events from .ics files, and subscriptions to calendar links.
The week grid fits your working day to the window, base16 color schemes import as themes, and Settings picks where places open from a menu.
Five more built-in themes: Paper, Minimal, Minimal Dark, Tomorrow and Tomorrow Night, with theme menus in Settings and readable invitations in light terminals.
A faster start, a full-screen calendar in the terminal, agenda colors from your theme, upgrade and downgrade commands, a note when a newer release is out, and tab completion for bash, zsh and fish.

Drag an event to the edge of the view to carry it to the next or previous week or month, tooltips with keyboard shortcuts, place settings that stay put, and changes to one occurrence of a repeating event that no longer ask about the whole series.
Installed Callie can connect Google accounts: earlier packages were built without the sign-in client they need.
A system tray entry while Callie keeps running, your working location (Home, Office) under each day's date, overlapping events laid out so every title shows, and a tidier event editor.

Change events as well as create them: edit times, repeats (custom ones too), places with search and maps, guests from your contacts and video calls, move whole series, and undo any change. Changes made offline wait and go once you are back.
Also new: search, an invitations tray, keyboard shortcuts with an optional vi mode, your own calendar names and colors, account photos, the callie command for more tasks, and developer settings.
The first release: a cozy calendar for Linux that keeps up with your Google calendars, with day, week, month and agenda views, quick add, invitations, themes and settings.
